title: Expected Nonhalting Bound from Round Decay
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x$ be a binary input, and let $s_0,R\in\mathbb{N}$ with $R>0$. Suppose there is a configuration $c_0$ such that every choice word of length $s_0$ reaches $c_0$ from the initial configuration on $x$. Let $a\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0\le a<1$, and suppose that for every $j\in\mathbb{N}$ the probability that a uniformly chosen length-$Rj$ choice word leaves the run from $c_0$ unhalted is at most $a^j$. Then, for every $K\in\mathbb{N}$, the sum over $t=0,\ldots,K-1$ of the probability that a uniformly chosen length-$t$ choice word leaves the run from the initial configuration on $x$ unhalted is at most $s_0+R/(1-a)$.
